verdict_vs_current.quote: The money is clearly better: you'd make roughly $380k more over 4 years, with most of it in the first two.

recommendation.quote: Whether to take it now depends on whether you actually want the job, plus a few terms to confirm before you sign.

refresh_valued_at.quote: That holds even if Google never gives you a refresh grant while your Meta numbers include Meta refreshes.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If you're not, walking away from a good offer is still fine.

final_decision.quote: If you're excited about the role and team at Google, take it once the terms above check out.

rsu_annualized.quote: New package: $240k base + $48k bonus (20%) + $1.08M in stock over 4 years + $200k sign-on bonus

year1_vs_recurring.quote: Almost all of the gain is one-time. Your ongoing pay at Google is about $558k a year, compared with about $526k at Meta.

forfeiture_netted.quote: you aren't really losing the $200k of Meta stock. Your Google grant starts vesting right away and replaces it, and the table already accounts for that.
